blocks.text: I can write a composite function both numerically and algebraically.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: The composition of functions is the process of combining two or more functions into a single function.
The composite function gf(x) is the combination of f(x) and g(x). The output from f(x) is the input for g(x).

blocks.text: f(x) = 4x and g(x) = 6x + 3. We can evaluate lots of things:
For 2f(5), the output of f(5) was multiplied by 2.
We can also evaluate gf(5). This is called a composite function: it is composed of two functions. The output of one function is the input of the other function.
For gf(5), the output of f(5) is substituted into the function g(x).
It works the other way too. For fg(8), the output of g(8) is substituted into the function f(x): fg(8) = f(g(8)) = f(51) = 4(51) = 204.

slides.title: fg is not the same as gf

blocks.text: In algebra ab means a × b, which is the same as b × a. But fg(x) and gf(x) are function notation.

items: fg(x) is the function f(x) happening to the output of g(x).
gf(x) is the function g(x) happening to the output of f(x).

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: You cannot work from left to right. Each function needs an input, and in a composite function the input has to be worked out first. For fg(x) you evaluate g first, then f.

blocks.label: Are fg(x) and gf(x) ever the same?
blocks.text: They are typically not the same thing, but there are exceptions: when the two functions are identical, f(x) = g(x), or when one function is the inverse of the other.

blocks.q: Match the notation to the correct language.

pairs.b: The output of g(4) being input into f(x)
The output of f(4) being input into g(x)
The output of g(4) being input into h(x)
The output of h(4) being input into g(x)

blocks.text: f(x) = 7x and g(x) = 2x − 6.
Notice that fg(3) = 0 but gf(3) = 36. The order matters.

blocks.q: f(x) = 5x and g(x) = x + 8. Evaluate each composite function.

blocks.text: Sometimes a function is composed of more than two functions. f(x) = 2x, g(x) = 5x and h(x) = 3x − 7. Evaluate fgh(4).
The output of h(4) is the input of g(x), and then the output of g(5) is the input of f(x).
We also see composite functions that use the same function again. f(x) = 5x + 3. The output of f(2) goes back into the same function f(x).

blocks.label: Show the working
blocks.text: hgf(1): f(1) = 5, the output goes into g: g(5) = 10, then into h: h(10) = 3(10) − 5 = 25. gg(3) = g(g(3)) = g(6) = 12.
Mathematicians are always seeking efficiency. If f(x) = 6x and g(x) = x − 5, working out fg(1), fg(2), fg(4) and so on means substituting into two functions each time.
We can write the algebraic form for the combined function: fg(x) = f(g(x)) = f(x − 5) = 6(x − 5).
Now we only substitute into one function: fg(1) = 6(1 − 5) = −24 and fg(4) = 6(4 − 5) = −6.
For gf(x) the output of f(x) goes into g(x): gf(x) = g(f(x)) = g(6x) = 6x − 5.
Now f(x) = x² − x and g(x) = x + 5. Then fg(x) = f(x + 5) = (x + 5)² − (x + 5).

blocks.label: Watch out for the minus!
blocks.text: We have to subtract both terms inside the bracket (x + 5): (x² + 10x + 25) − x − 5 = x² + 9x + 20.

blocks.q: f(x) = 3x and g(x) = x + 4. Which is the correct expression?
f(x) = x² + 2x and g(x) = x − 1. What is fg(x) after expanding and simplifying?

items: A composite function combines two or more functions: in gf(x), the output from f(x) is the input for g(x).
fg(x) and gf(x) are not necessarily the same thing.
A composite function can be evaluated numerically, for example fg(1), as well as expressed algebraically.
For example, if f(x) = 9x and g(x) = x − 8 we can evaluate fg(1) or fg(2) or any other numerical input, and we can also write an expression for fg(x).

flashcards.back: The combination of two functions. In gf(x), the output from f(x) is the input for g(x).
The process of combining two or more functions into a single function.

flashcards.front: In fg(x), which function happens first?
flashcards.back: g. The function f happens to the output of g(x): fg(x) = f(g(x)).

flashcards.front: Are fg(x) and gf(x) usually the same?
flashcards.back:
No, not in most cases.

They are the same if f(x) = g(x), or if one function is the inverse of the other.

flashcards.front: Why can’t you work a composite function from left to right?
flashcards.back: Each function needs an input, and in a composite function the input has to be worked out first.

flashcards.front: In fgh(4), in which order are the functions used?
flashcards.back: h first, then g, then f: fgh(4) = f(g(h(4))).

flashcards.front: f(x) = 6x and g(x) = x − 5. Write fg(x) as one function.
f(x) = 6x and g(x) = x − 5. Write gf(x) as one function.
Why write a composite function as one algebraic function?
flashcards.back: It is more efficient: you only have to substitute into one function.

flashcards.front: f(x) = x² − x and g(x) = x + 5. What is fg(x)?
flashcards.back:
(x + 5)² − (x + 5) = x² + 10x + 25 − x − 5 = x² + 9x + 20

Subtract both terms inside the bracket.
